title: JPMorgan Rethinks UK Investments: Will Higher Taxes Hurt Growth? - TradingView
content: JPMorgan JPM is reportedly reconsidering its planned investments in the United Kingdom as higher banking taxes threaten to weigh on profitability. The bank is evaluating potential spending reductions at its Bournemouth operations center and approximately £5 billion Canary Wharf development in London. However, neither project is likely to be abandoned. The development follows CEO Jamie Dimon's Nov. 20 remarks about offsetting the financial impact of higher taxes. The U.K. banking surcharge is set to double from 3% to 6% for 15 months, beginning January 2027. The measure could increase JPMorgan's tax bill by £120 million, affecting after-tax earnings and investment returns. Potential spending reductions underscore the company's focus on disciplined capital allocation and expense management. Scaling back infrastructure investments could help preserve cash flows and moderate future operating costs. JPMorgan may also reassess the geographical allocation of incremental investments, prioritizing markets offering more attractive risk-adjusted returns. However, significantly curtailing U.K. investments could pose challenges. London remains a major global financial hub, offering access to institutional clients, skilled professionals and international capital markets. Reduced spending could limit JPMorgan's ability to expand operational capacity and capitalize on emerging business opportunities in the region. JPMorgan's diversified revenue streams and robust earnings generation provide flexibility to absorb incremental tax costs. While disciplined spending could cushion the financial impact, prolonged tax uncertainty and reduced infrastructure investments may constrain international expansion. Management's ability to balance expense optimization with strategic investments will remain crucial to sustaining long-term earnings growth and shareholder returns. JPMorgan’s Peers & Their Global Expansion Initiatives Two key peers of JPM are Bank of America BAC and Goldman Sachs GS. Bank of America is strengthening its international presence through strategic hiring and broader corporate banking coverage. Bank of America has doubled its corporate banking team across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, targeting 40% client growth in the region to capitalize on cross-border financing and advisory opportunities. Goldman continues to strengthen its international operations through workforce expansion across key financial and technology hubs. Goldman added 142 employees to its European banking operations over the past year, while its Indian workforce exceeds 8,000, supporting global operational capabilities and business expansion. title: Euro-to-Dollar Forecast Cut at J.P. Morgan on U.S. 'Yield Supremacy' - Pound Sterling Live
content: J.P. Morgan has lowered its euro-to-dollar forecast in its freshly published 2027 outlook and now looks for further losses, after a month in which the pair fell to its lowest level since April 2025. "Stay bullish USD particularly vs. low-yielding FX given intensifying yield supremacy. Yield spreads expected to widen to their highest since the 1980s with USD yielding more than ~60% of currencies globally," says a new FX market analysis from the U.S. investment bank. J.P. Morgan's rate forecasts point to that gap widening in the dollar's favour against the euro: in a note published on 21 November it forecast three consecutive quarter-point rate rises at the Federal Reserve, in December, January and March. Its 2027 outlook sees the European Central Bank raising rates in December and March, then holding its deposit rate at 3.00% through the end of 2027. Morgan now forecasts EUR/USD at 1.05 over the coming year on the widening U.S. yield advantage, down from the 1.10 it forecast for September 2027 in its 21 November note. Investors earn more on U.S. bonds as the gap over euro area interest rates widens, so they sell euros to buy dollars, which pulls EUR/USD lower. The earlier forecast sat just above spot at 1.0967, so the revision turns a call for little change into one for a further fall of around 4%. Above: EUR/USD at daily intervals over the past 12 months, with J.P. Morgan's 1.05 forecast as the dashed line. EUR/USD has already fallen almost 10% this year, from a 2026 high of 1.2081 on 27 January to 1.0881 on 23 November. BCA Research also targets 1.05 but sees a brief rally to 1.12 first, with the euro not yet cheap enough to buy and the slide to 1.05 coming "before the real opportunity emerges," says the independent research house. J.P. Morgan's own risk case is a faster sell-off in AI stocks: "Risk is if AI unwind accelerates as years of international inflows into USD corporate assets are poorly hedged," says the bank. Overseas investors who bought U.S. shares and bonds without protecting themselves against a fall in the dollar would have to sell dollars if they pulled their money out, which would weigh on the currency. Nomura goes further and forecasts EUR/USD at 1.25 in twelve months, because it sees little room left for markets to raise their bets on Fed hikes or to push up U.S. Treasury yields, the return on U.S. government bonds: "upward pressure on USD is likely to peak before long," says the Japanese investment bank in a recent update. Nomura's call runs against the chart picture at J.P. Morgan, where EUR/USD "retains a bearish medium-term trend bias while below the 1.1273-1.1411 pattern breakdown area," says Jason Hunter, Cross-Asset Technical Strategist at J.P. Morgan. That zone is where the pair broke lower, and it now acts as resistance, a level where sellers can be expected to halt any recovery. Hunter puts support at 1.0882, a retracement level next to the 1.0881 low of 23 November, where buyers stepped in to halt the fall. A break below it would open the way to 1.0763, the first target implied by the chart pattern Hunter identifies, and a step towards J.P. Morgan's 1.05 forecast. title: Values: The quiet architecture of a family’s legacy - J.P. Morgan Private Bank
content:
The Private Bank’s mission is to build, preserve & transform our client’s wealth. We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Our world-class economists, strategists, and investment specialists share their timely ideas and perspectives. We have worked with clients for more than 200 years to help them achieve their unique ambitions. How does a legacy shape the future? By focusing on values outside the business, families can establish meaning for the next generation while remaining true to what’s gone before. Legacy is one of those words we tend to associate with the end of things; with wills, foundations and the appraisal of a life. But in the families I work with every day, I’ve come to see legacy very differently. It is not built at the end. Rather, it is built every day, in small decisions, conversations around a table and the stories we choose to tell our children. And at the heart of legacy, doing most of the work, are our own values. Values are our highest priorities as a family. They are the principles that shape how we make decisions, how we treat each other and how we show up in the world. What we believe slowly shapes what we think, say, do and repeat, until our habits become who we are and, eventually, what we leave behind. They are not abstract ideals, but the slow accumulation of everything a family does. And the question of whether that accumulation gets passed on has never been more pressing than it is right now. As J.P. Morgan’s Global Family Office Report highlights, a meaningful share of families still lack a structured approach to succession and preparing the rising generation, just as the largest intergenerational wealth transfer in history gets underway. The defining question is not only if the wealth will transfer, but will the values transfer with it? Shared values can help to keep a family cohesive when it disperses across cities and countries. They can turn inspiration and motivation into practice, through investment decisions, distributions and governance. And they can help answer the question every family eventually faces: “Why do we choose to stay together?” These are the reasons values matter. But how they actually move from one generation to the next is a different question, and the answer is rarely found in a document. One of the loveliest illustrations of this comes from an earlier generation of a Brazilian industrial family. When the grandchildren were little, their grandfather would take them to the family’s sugar mills in Brazil, stop them in front of the molasses and say, “You have to smell this.” Years later, one of the grandchildren, looking back, said simply, “He taught us to be passionate about the business.” He didn’t sit them down for a lecture or hand them a mission statement. He put them in front of the molasses and let them feel what the family was about. Values don’t travel on their own — somebody has to hand them over with intention. That handing over, though, is only the first act. What the next generation receives is never quite what the one before meant to give, and that is not a flaw of the process. It is the design. Inherit, interpret, contribute: How each generation can shape the legacy Many families get stuck thinking of values as a one-way street from one generation to the next. In reality, legacy moves in three directions at once: we inherit values, interpret them for the reality we live in and we contribute our own. Take the value of giving back. A founder’s version might be deeply personal: a hand in a drawer, and anyone who needed help got help. There were no forms and no committee, just a handshake and a decision. The next generation, with a bigger family and bigger needs, gives the value new shape, perhaps by establishing a family foundation. In this instance, the value has remained the same, but is now in a new form. And the generation after that can add to it, bringing impact investing, or focusing the foundation on climate change or mental health. These are causes their grandparents might never have named, yet the value travels and the expression evolves. That is not a betrayal of what came before, but how legacy stays alive. Interpretation is one thing. But every so often, a generation does something more significant than reshape an existing value — it adds a new one. Imagine a family that has run for generations on a very clear set of principles. Those principles built the business and held the family together, and for a long time they were enough. But at some point, a new generation looks around and sees that the world has changed. The family has grown, the children have set up their lives elsewhere, and the business is no longer the centre of daily life in the way it once was. And the family asks itself an honest question: what is actually missing? The business values may be solid, but if the next generation only inherits the values of the enterprise, will that be enough to make being part of the family feel like a gift, and not a responsibility?  The answer, in families who do this well, is almost always the same. They add a new value that has nothing to do with the business. Perhaps something about the way they interact with each other, or simply how to continue enjoy being a family. And then they live it, through customs, gatherings and small practices that make the new value visible in daily life. The old values do not go anywhere, the new is simply added — not imposed or forced — because the next generation saw something the one before could not quite see yet. Which brings us, naturally, to the generation most likely to be reading this with a question of their own: is it really my place to add something? The short answer is yes. You are not only the guardians of what came before, you are the co-authors of what comes next. Your tools, causes and vocabulary will be different from your grandparents’, and that is the point. Honour what came before, interpret it for your reality and then contribute your chapter. This is how legacy stays alive. Values, in the end, are the quiet architecture of a family’s legacy. They don’t show up on a balance sheet, and they don’t appear in a trust document unless we deliberately put them there. They live in the stories we tell and the rituals we repeat. It may simply be the charitable reach into the drawer of a desk, or the molasses we ask our children to smell, but values only travel from one generation to the next when somebody, on purpose, hands them over. The question each of us gets to answer is simple: what are my values, and how can I pass them on? What responsibilities come with generational stewardship? Generational stewardship means more than preserving wealth or managing an inheritance. It asks each generation to learn the family’s values, carry them forward through conversations, shared rituals and stories, and put them into practice when making decisions. Younger family members can take part by asking questions, seeking guidance, and contributing their skills and ideas. In turn, they help ensure that future generations inherit not only assets, but also a meaningful role in shaping what comes next. How do families pass values to the next generation? A sixth-generation Brazilian industrial family shows that values aren’t taught through lectures but transmitted through lived experience, like a grandfather bringing grandchildren to smell molasses at the family’s sugar mills to instil passion for the business. It’s a powerful reminder that legacy is handed over through intentional moments, not mission statements. What does a meaningful family legacy looks like for the rising generation? A meaningful legacy means the rising generation isn’t just inheriting values passively—they’re co-authors who interpret family principles for today’s world and contribute entirely new values, like prioritising relationships and joy alongside business success. True legacy stays alive when each generation adds its own chapter. Why are family values important across generations? Values create the shared language and cohesion that hold a family together, especially as members disperse across cities and countries—they answer the fundamental question of “why do we choose to stay together?” Without explicit, shared values, even the largest wealth transfer risks losing the family identity that gave it meaning. How can each generation inherit, interpret and contribute to family values? Legacy moves in three directions: each generation inherits values from those before, interprets them to fit new realities (like turning a founder’s personal generosity into a family foundation), and contributes entirely new values the prior generation couldn’t yet see. This continuous cycle—not a one-way handoff—is what keeps a family’s legacy evolving and alive. Many families capture their values in a family values statement, a family mission statement or a family constitution. Writing values down creates a shared language across generations and helps carry them into investment decisions, distributions, philanthropy and family governance. The statements that last are usually drafted together, revisited over time and reflected in everyday practices. title: Year-end planning: 10 actions to consider before 2027 - J.P. Morgan Private Bank

We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Our world-class economists, strategists, and investment specialists share their timely ideas and perspectives. We have worked with clients for more than 200 years to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Are you doing everything you can to enhance your financial well-being—and help manage your 2026 taxes? Careful review of your financial picture before year end can help you make the most of these 10 planning strategies in 2027 and beyond. Having ample time to review your balance sheet and your personal and financial goals for the coming year will allow you to make thoughtful adjustments before January 1, if needed. An early start will also make it easier to involve your personal and professional advisors in the process. Establish or update a structured decision-making framework for your investments and goals. This can help provide clarity and consistency to ensure that your goals are aligned with your financial resources. Ask your J.P. Morgan team about our proprietary Goals-Based planning tool to help analyze your risk exposure and cash flows and position your balance sheet to support your investment, spending and gifting objectives and make decisions. We expect the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates once this year, by 25 basis points, before holding rates steady for some time. Short-duration instruments and laddered structures can potentially offer attractive yields today while keeping you positioned to extend when yields peak. Other planning moves to consider: Review all policies, including term coverage, to make sure they still meet the initial intent and if any changes need to be made.  Among the things to review, check: Ask your accountant for an approximation of what your 2026 taxes due will be, based on the information to date. This “pro forma” can inform decisions about whether to accelerate or delay the recognition of deductible items. Consider asking your J.P. Morgan team for a “tax summary”, based on your account information to help with your tax estimates. With your tax snapshot in hand, you can better assess if it makes sense to implement tax planning strategies before year-end. Consider harvesting tax losses (and maybe some gains) Tax-loss harvesting is a classic strategy that may reduce your tax liability.1 Tax loss harvesting involves selling an investment at a loss. This loss can help offset either already-realized gains, or embedded gains that you realize now or in the future. Be careful not to violate any “wash sale rule” in your home jurisdiction. Such rules may prevent investors from taking a loss if they buy a substantially identical or similar security within a certain amount of time before or after the trade. Some countries already impose wealth or inheritance taxes, while others have been discussing them for years. Now is a good time to look at your balance sheet and decide if there are assets you want to transfer to younger family members or to charity. You may  consider whether irrevocable trusts are appropriate for your family members.2 These trusts may be for children and grandchildren, or continue for many generations. Speak with your attorneys and your J.P. Morgan wealth advisor about strategies to transfer wealth to the next generation. Review existing estate planning documents, such as wills and trusts, to confirm they reflect your current wishes and family circumstances. Carefully plan trust distributions to ensure they’re as tax efficient as possible. If making gifts to family members living in the U.S., be mindful of gifting any U.S. tangible property, including cash, which could trigger U.S. gift tax. For charitable gifts, review your year-end gifting strategy and whether you can take a charitable deduction for your gifts. There are many ways to give to charity, from direct gifts, to donor advised funds, or your own foundation. Establishing a plan for giving can help your charitable dollars have the most impact. Keep in mind that some assets may take longer to transfer. Make sure any donation process begins early enough to be deemed complete by December 31. It's never too early to begin talking with your children and grandchildren about money, family values, and the responsibilities that can come with wealth.  These conversations do not need to be formal or overly complex.  They can begin in simple, natural ways — a discussion around the dinner table, sharing stories behind the family’s history, talking about how wealth can support a meaningful life, or by choosing a charitable gift together. Year-end gatherings can provide a good opportunity to be more intentional, turning time together into a chance to strengthen communication, build understanding, and help younger generations feel more prepared over time. For some families, this may evolve into a more structured family meeting; for others, the goal may simply be to create a regular rhythm of open and honest communication. Either way, these moments can help build trust, confidence, and a sense of shared purpose well before any formal transfer of responsibility takes place. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) apps and tools continue to become integrated into daily life, it's crucial to actively protect your data and privacy, especially from social engineering threats. Here are steps to take now: With an active IPO market in 2026, many families are navigating significant new liquidity events—or preparing for ones on the horizon. Whether you are part of a company that recently completed its IPO, hold stock in a pre-IPO company, or manage a portfolio heavily weighted to a single position, this is the time to evaluate your exposure and goals. Depending on your restrictions and tax situation, consider 10b5-1 trading plans, or charitable strategies to help manage single-stock risk in a tax-efficient manner. If you received new equity awards this year, review the vesting schedule, the tax treatment at vesting versus exercise and whether you have awards approaching expiration that require action. If you were granted stock options, understand the financial impact of exercising your options and develop an exercise strategy before the options expire. For those with post-IPO lockup expirations approaching, consider your options and liquidity needs, and develop a plan early to make decisions based on your ultimate intent. Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) closed at $109.51 on Nov. 24, 56% below its June 1 high. But on Nov. 23, J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee reiterated his Buy rating and $200 price target, 83% above that close. S&P says OpenAI accounts for about half of Oracle's backlog, while OpenAI's latest funding round has reached only half of its $30 billion target, CNBC reported. In August, J.P. That's hardly heroic. Oracle traded between 12x and 17x from 2014 to early 2021, when its revenue grew about 1% a year, and analysts now expect revenue to nearly double from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028. The catch is the debt. Oracle says free cash flow tops $30 billion in fiscal 2029, while analysts expect $17.5 billion. And on Nov. 25, the cost of insuring Oracle's debt hit a record, alongside CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ), whose spread implies a 68% chance of default within five years. Until credit markets stop lumping the two together, a higher multiple will be hard to earn. Still, I think J.P. Morgan has this one right. title: JP Morgan Outlines Oil Outlook for 2027, 2028 - Rigzone
content:
In a new report sent to Rigzone by Natasha Kaneva, J.P. Morgan’s Head of Global Commodities Strategy, analysts at the company, including Kaneva, outlined J.P. Morgan’s oil outlook for 2027 and 2028. The J.P. Morgan analysts revealed in the report that their outlook assumes the U.S.-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts continue, “yet oil keeps moving and the global market remains in surplus”. “If 2022 and 2026 have taught us anything, it is that wars can disrupt oil flows without stopping them,” the analysts said in the report. “We are therefore modeling a world in which two wars continue, but oil keeps moving,” they added. The analysts highlighted in the report that, “with crude flowing and demand contracting, the global oil market returned to surplus in September”. They pointed out that this excess widened in October and that China has already begun rebuilding its crude inventories, “adding 400,000 barrels per day in October” with the country “on pace to add another 500,000 barrels per day in November”. “We expect that surplus to persist into 2027,” the analysts revealed. “Our forecast assumes Middle Eastern oil flows remain near 90 percent of pre-war levels through March, rising to 94 percent by June and 98 percent by year-end, while demand returns sustainably to pre-war volumes by August,” they added. “China is expected to rebuild crude inventories at an average pace of nearly 700,000 barrels per day, with OECD countries adding another 400,000 barrels per day,” they projected. They warned, however, that, even after accounting for this stock-building, they project a global surplus of 1.6 million barrels per day, “consistent with a Brent price in the high $70s in the first half of the year and the high $60s in the second”. The analysts went on to warn that this surplus will not disappear in 2028. “Even assuming China accelerates inventory accumulation to 1.1 million barrels per day and OECD countries continue adding 0.4 million barrels per day, we expect the market to remain oversupplied by roughly 1.4 million barrels per day, implying a Brent price in the mid-$60s,” they said. “That is our fundamentally driven price forecast, not necessarily the price at which oil will trade throughout the year,” the analysts highlighted, noting that further escalations “could inject substantial geopolitical risk premia into the market”. The J.P. Morgan analysts revealed in the report that they are reluctant to forecast those premia, “let alone embed them permanently into our price outlook”. “History suggests they can be large, but rarely last,” they pointed out. “Since 2005, monthly Brent prices have never exceeded our estimated fair value by more than $24 per barrel, with such deviations lasting an average of just 3.8 months,” they said. “Two wars may keep oil prices volatile. But unless they materially alter the physical balance, the underlying surplus should ultimately prevail,” they projected. The J.P. Morgan analysts highlighted in the report that a “flood of supply is coming”, pointing out that global liquids production “is projected to surge by nearly eight million barrels per day in 2027, reaching 109 million barrels per day, before climbing to 110 million barrels per day by year-end and remaining near that level in 2028”. In their report, the analysts outlined that the U.S.-Iran conflict “has acted like a dam, holding back Middle Eastern production for months”. “Once the barriers are lifted, the rush to reclaim lost market share could unleash a flood of additional supply, particularly from producers outside Iran,” they projected. “By March 2027, we expect Middle Eastern supply outside of Iran to have fully recovered to its 2025 average, before rising further,” they said. The Middle East will not be alone in driving supply growth, according to the analysts, who projected that the Americas are set to add another 1.6 million barrels per day to supply, led by a 0.5 million barrel per day increase in U.S. total liquids production. “Brazil should contribute another 0.5 million barrels per day, as three new floating production, storage and offloading vessels come online, with output expected to keep rising through 2031,” they said. “Guyana should add 0.3 million barrels per day, while Canada and Argentina will contribute another 0.1 and 0.2 million barrels per day, respectively,” they added. “Importantly, much of the growth in Brazil and Guyana comes from deep-water projects, where production is relatively insensitive to oil prices and unlikely to slow even if prices weaken,” they continued. The analysts went on to warn that Russia “remains the main geopolitical variable”. “Assuming the war in Ukraine continues without a resolution, we expect Russian production to average 8.7 million barrels per day next year, broadly unchanged from current levels,” they said. “A ceasefire, however, could lift output to 9.4 million barrels per day, adding another 0.7 million barrels per day to global supply,” they added. “Put these numbers together, and the scale of the recovery becomes extraordinary. After plunging from 107 million barrels per day in 2025 to 101 million barrels per day in 2026, global liquids production is poised to surge to 109 million barrels per day in 2027,” they noted. “That is nearly eight million barrels per day of additional supply in a single year, more than reversing the losses of 2026 and leaving the world producing two million barrels per day more oil than before the war,” they added. “In just twelve months, the world could emerge from one of the largest supply disruptions in history with more oil than it had going into it,” they continued. “And the recovery is unlikely to stop there”, the analysts emphasized. “We project global oil supply to reach 110 million barrels per day by the end of 2027 and remain near that level throughout 2028 - some three million barrels per day above its 2025 average and an extraordinary nine million barrels per day above 2019 levels,” they added. The J.P. Morgan analysts projected in the report that oil demand will rebound but said refining capacity will set the ceiling for this comeback. “Oil consumption could theoretically recover by 4.5 million barrels per day in 2027 but meeting that demand would require global refinery runs to increase by 4.1 million barrels per day relative to 2026, against an expected gain of just 3.3 million barrels per day,” they said. “Refining constraints will keep product cracks and prices elevated, limiting demand growth to 3.5 million barrels per day, just 0.6 million barrels per day above pre-war levels,” they added. The analysts went on to reveal in the report that, “with demand data now available through September”, they estimate that global oil consumption has fallen by 3.0 million barrels per day this year. “Nearly half of that decline - 1.3 million barrels per day - came from petrochemical feedstocks, as physical shortages forced refiners to cut runs, particularly in Asia,” they said. “The rest was largely a response to record-high regional prices for refined products, rather than crude oil itself, with diesel demand falling by 0.8 million barrels per day, gasoline by 0.5 million barrels per day and jet fuel by 0.1 million barrels per day,” they added. “The Middle East, at the center of the conflict, saw consumption fall by 0.9 million barrels per day, while China and the rest of Asia each lost roughly 0.8 million barrels per day as shortages and soaring product prices took their toll,” they continued. “The impact eventually spread to developed economies, including Europe, where consumption contracted by 0.28 million barrels per day and the U.S., where it declined by 0.13 million barrels per day,” they noted. The analysts stated in the report that “why consumption fell matters enormously for what comes next”. “If demand has fallen primarily because oil products were unavailable or prohibitively expensive, much of that consumption should return once supplies normalize and prices retreat,” they said. “And although the conflict is now in its ninth month, we doubt it has lasted long enough to fundamentally reshape consumption patterns,” they added. “Still, there is a limit to how much stretching even a rubber band can withstand. The longer consumers are forced to adapt to shortages and high prices, the greater the risk that some of those adjustments will become permanent,” they continued. The J.P. Morgan analysts said in the report that, “for now”, their “natural inclination is to follow the conventional logic of hysteresis”. “After major economic shocks and disruptions, oil consumption tends to recover toward its previous level, but the subsequent growth trajectory becomes shallower. In other words, the level of demand recovers, but some of its future growth is lost,” they added. The mechanism for that recovery is relatively straightforward, according to the analysts. “As damaged refining capacity returns and refinery runs normalize, product shortages should ease, refining cracks should retreat and trade flows recover,” they said. “Lower product prices, in turn, should encourage consumption that was previously constrained by either availability or affordability,” they added. “Following this logic, global oil demand could in theory rebound like a coiled spring, surging by as much as 4.5 million barrels per day in 2027, lifting consumption 1.5 million barrels per day above its pre-war level,” they continued. “But here is the rub - the world may have more than enough crude oil to meet demand, but not enough refining capacity to turn it into the products consumers actually need,” they warned. The analysts highlighted that accommodating the additional 1.5 million barrels per day of consumption would require global refinery runs to increase by 1.1 million barrels per day relative to 2025. “Yet global refining capacity is expected to increase by just 0.97 million barrels per day - enough to support an increase in runs of only about 200,000 barrels per day,” they said. “The resulting mismatch between rebounding demand and constrained processing capacity would push gasoline, diesel and jet fuel cracks higher, raising prices for the very products whose soaring costs drove demand down in the first place,” they warned. After accounting for the volume of crude that refiners “can realistically process”, the analysts estimated in the report that global oil demand in 2027 could rise by a maximum of 0.58 million barrels per day above 2025 levels, equivalent to a recovery of 3.5 million barrels per day from 2026. In a BMI report sent to Rigzone by the Fitch Group recently, analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, projected that energy prices are set to fall “as scarcity shifts to oversupply, while refined fuel prices remain elevated”. “After a preliminary U.S.-Iran deal is reached, regional oil and gas flows will rise, paving the way for strong gains in global crude and natural gas exports,” the BMI analysts projected in this report. “As supply growth overwhelms demand, the market will tip into surplus, driving steep and broad-based declines in energy prices,” they added. “That said, global fuel prices will stay elevated into 2027 as refining constraints and record-low inventories keep markets undersupplied, despite improving Strait of Hormuz trade flows and possible extra Mainland Chinese exports,” they continued. The analysts warned in the report that the year 2027 will mark a “sharp reversal” for energy commodities, “as fading geopolitical risk premia and a surge in supply drive steep price declines across the complex”. “The U.S.-Iran war has been the dominant factor behind 2026’s rally, and our core view sees Washington and Tehran reach a preliminary deal in Q1 2027, triggering a sharp sell-off in oil and gas prices,” they said. “As the maritime security environment improves and the Strait of Hormuz reopens, regional flows will normalize in full, unlocking volumes constrained since the outbreak of the conflict,” they added. The BMI analysts noted that Middle Eastern Gulf crude oil producers were operating around seven million barrels per day below capacity as of October 2026 and revealed that they are forecasting that regional production will rise by 5.59 million barrels per day year on year in 2027, “alongside a further 2.10 million barrels per day of growth elsewhere, with the U.S. leading the gains”. “That expansion will comfortably outstrip the recovery in oil demand,” they warned. “Lower energy costs, improving economic conditions, higher Asian refinery utilization and the rebuilding of depleted inventories will absorb some of the additional barrels, but only temporarily, while structural trends towards efficiency, fuel-switching and electrification continue to cap consumption growth,” they projected. The analysts revealed in the report that they expect Brent to average $112 per barrel in Q1 2027 before dropping to $67 per barrel by Q4 2027, averaging $81 per barrel over 2027, “down from $93 per barrel in 2026”. They warned, however, that they are already seeing “strong downside risks to this forecast” which they said they are likely to revise down in the coming weeks. “The emerging glut will test OPEC+’s ability to manage the market and, with the imbalance unlikely to clear in 2028, we forecast Brent to average around $70 per barrel over 2028-2030, with risks tilted towards a deeper downturn,” they said in the report. The BMI analysts projected that refined fuels will fall in tandem but forecasted that “the slower recovery in Middle Eastern downstream operations and continued disruption to Russian refining will keep product cracks historically elevated”. “The same dynamics will play out in gas, as recovering Middle Eastern LNG exports coincide with nearly 95 million tons per annum (mtpa) of new liquefaction capacity by end-2027, pushing global gas markets into prolonged surplus,” they noted. In the report, the BMI analysts went on to highlight that global fuel prices are expected to remain elevated as refining capacity constraints continue to limit supply growth against record-low inventories. “The availability of global refined fuels should continue to steadily improve with increased trade flows emanating from the Strait of Hormuz over the early quarters of 2027, although fundamentals will remain tilted to undersupply, full normalization of pre-conflict trade remains elusive, and Russian refining capacity remains disrupted,” they said. “Mainland China’s increasing fuel exports may give markets some additional supply relief, but limited fuel exports to end-2026 hint at continued restraint for 2027,” they warned. “Diesel, gasoline and jet fuel prices are al forecast to ease from their 2026 peaks but remain elevated through 2027 as refining constraints and depleted inventories keep markets undersupplied,” they added. The analysts outlined in the report that a preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement reopening the Strait of Hormuz in Q1 2027 would support a gradual improvement in product availability but said full normalization of pre-conflict trade flows “will take longer given depleted inventories and constrained refining capacity”. “Additional Mainland Chinese fuel exports could offer some supply relief, but limited export volumes to end-2026 point to continued restraint into 2027,” they projected. title: HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX complete first live trades using Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) - Kitco
content: Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments. (Kitco News) – Gold’s digital evolution passed a major milestone on Tuesday after HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX conducted wholesale-market transactions using Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) for the first time. PGI is the underpinning of the World Gold Council’s Wholesale Digital Gold initiative, and Tuesday’s pilot transactions represent a significant step towards a new way for institutions to own, transfer and use gold. “Loco London physical 400-ounce Good Delivery gold bars were placed into the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem, and PGI were created, giving participants proprietary interests over pooled gold,” the WGC said in its announcement. “Once the transactions were settled, the gold was withdrawn from the ecosystem, completing the full lifecycle.” ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) acted as the operator for the transactions, and Baton Systems was the technology provider. “Today, Wholesale Digital Gold moved from concept to reality,” said David Tait, Chief Executive Officer of the World Gold Council. “For the first time, leading institutions have transferred, settled and used fractional ownership of physical gold as collateral through real, live transactions. This is a historic step forward for the gold market, preserving trust in physical ownership while opening up new ways for gold to be used in modern financial markets.” “J.P. Morgan is one of the largest and most active participants in the global precious metals market, with a presence that spans trading, clearing, vaulting and financing across every major hub,” said Mark Amlin, Global Head of Physical Commodities at J.P. Morgan. “That global footprint gives us a clear view of where the market’s infrastructure needs to evolve. Gold ownership that is fractional, readily transferable and insolvency remote would allow gold to be used more widely across financial markets, including as collateral.” Richard Anthony, Global Head of Macro eRisk and Precious Metals at HSBC, noted that the London-based bank has been participating in the precious metals market for more than 160 years since its founding in Hong Kong, and remains one of the world’s largest gold custodians and clearers. “We continue to invest in technology, including our gold tokenisation capabilities, to enable our clients to have greater access to gold,” Anthony said. “Developing a modern digital infrastructure for gold ownership and settlement is important to the overall market.” Michael Skinner, Global Head of Metals at StoneX, said the firm was pleased to have been involved in the Wholesale Digital Gold initiative from the outset. “StoneX has invested consistently in developing new solutions across commodities markets, from vaulting and refining through to execution and clearing, and we support initiatives like this one because they have the potential to deliver materially better outcomes for our clients — greater flexibility, lower operational friction and more efficient use of capital,” he said. The Wholesale Digital Gold initiative aims to address a longstanding challenge for the industry: how to preserve the integrity and trust of physical gold ownership while making gold easier to trade and use across modern financial markets. The WGC said this pilot demonstrates how digitalization can help gold move more efficiently through financial markets. The initiative was first launched in September 2025 in the white paper Pooled Gold Interests and Wholesale Digital Gold – A New Vision for the Gold Market. FILE PHOTO: The SpaceX logo in this illustration taken June 11, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo Nov 24 (Reuters) - A potential merger of SpaceX and Tesla <TSLA.O> could make the rocket company eligible for the S&P 500 and trigger passive buying of roughly 10% of its free-float shares, J.P. Morgan said in a note on Tuesday. S&P will adjust SpaceX’s float-adjusted market capitalization as lock-up periods expire and shares become available for trading, J.P. Morgan said, potentially speeding the company’s entry into some S&P Dow Jones indexes. • The two public companies, both led by Elon Musk, have appointed five directors, three from Tesla and two from SpaceX, to guide two special committees handling merger negotiations, media reports said • SpaceX is currently not eligible for inclusion in the S&P 500 because it would need 12 months of trading after its market debut and positive net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in its latest quarter and over the trailing 12 months • If a merger with Tesla goes through, historical precedent suggests the S&P Dow Jones committee could waive certain eligibility requirements, J.P. Morgan analysts said • In June, the index provider said it would modify entry rules for its broader S&P Total Market Index and Dow Jones US Total Stock Market Index, creating a pathway for SpaceX to join those less widely followed indexes • The brokerage said S&P confirmed it will increase SpaceX's float-adjusted market capitalization at intervals, bringing it closer to levels that could be reflected in the S&P 500 • J.P. Morgan estimates SpaceX's entry into these indexes would accelerate passive buying that had previously been expected no earlier than September 2027 (Reporting by Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid) Sorry, there are no recent results for popular images. On November 24, Gupta maintained the bank’s 12-month price target for Tesla stock at $430. As TSLA traded at $386.46 at the time of writing, the bank signals a possible 11.55% upside over the next 12 months. The ‘Neutral’ rating on Tesla was based on the initial rollout of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) version 15, highlighting that the update solidifies the company’s competitive advantage in consumer autonomy. Furthermore, the software introduces a redesigned artificial intelligence (AI) architecture, which is shared across other products including Robotaxi and Optimus. The highest Tesla stock price target for the next 12 months is $550, while the lowest is $24.86. More Wall Street analysts are bullish on the company over the coming months, driven by advanced merger talks with Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX). Notably, SpaceX and Tesla could be seeking to combine their AI synergy to strengthen their competitive edge. At the time of publication, Tesla stock had soared 11.46%, thereby increasing the company’s market capitalization to $1.52 trillion. Over the last 52 weeks, TSLA’s price ranged between $498.82 and $297.38. Consequently, JPMorgan joined other Wall Street analysts in predicting that Tesla stock could not rally to a new all-time high again in the next 12 months. title: Philanthropy is being transformed: New approaches to effective giving - J.P. Morgan Private Bank
content:
The Private Bank’s mission is to build, preserve & transform our client’s wealth. We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Our world-class economists, strategists, and investment specialists share their timely ideas and perspectives. We have worked with clients for more than 200 years to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Profound change is unfolding across philanthropy, largely driven by three converging forces: The sector is responding with greater flexibility, collaboration and purpose. Here's what you need to know: The starting point for most nonprofits, donors and foundations is using AI to improve research, streamline operations, handle day-to-day communications and speed up grantmaking. Even at this early stage, we see AI fundamentally changing how donors give and manage philanthropic activities. A 2025 survey of more than 751 social sector leaders across four European nations found 48% of nonprofits and foundations already use AI tools, citing fundraising and operational efficiency as the main drivers.2 As one example, a family foundation has developed a free, AI-powered tool for grantmakers that streamlines financial due diligence — typically a resource- and time-intensive task. It analyses a grant-seeker's financial records, including audited statements, and generates a scorecard against criteria the grantmaker selects, while making it easy for nonprofits to submit their documents.3 Foundations and nonprofits using AI share common concerns: data security and privacy, accuracy, ethics, and the loss of sector skills and jobs.4 Yet few have put guardrails in place to protect stakeholder trust. In response, many funders are supporting safe, equitable and ethical AI development. One such effort, led by The European AI & Society Fund, works to align AI with democratic values and the public interest. Backed by prominent European philanthropic organisations, it uses strategic grants to help civil society groups advocate for ethical AI, promote transparency and safeguard human rights.5 As AI advances in philanthropy, balancing innovation with oversight will be key to serving the greater good. Today's most effective funders recognise that the way they give is just as important as how much they give. Responsive philanthropy reimagines the relationship between donors, nonprofits and communities, rebalancing power and decision-making to benefit all parties. For nonprofits, reduced administrative burdens and the trust to deploy resources where needed build resilience and free staff to focus on mission. For funders, the rewards are equally compelling: deeper insight, stronger partnerships and greater confidence that capital is well deployed. The result is a more effective and equitable ecosystem where well-supported organisations deliver lasting impact. Simple steps funders can take to better support the communities they serve: Spotlight: The Esmée Fairbairn Foundation is a leading UK trust-based funder committed to improving the natural world, securing a fairer future and nurturing creative communities. By providing long-term, unrestricted funding and building strong grantee relationships, it enables organisations to focus on their mission rather than funder requirements. Through larger grants to a smaller portfolio of partners, it deepens its support and increases their capacity to deliver lasting change.6 As you consider how to embed more responsive philanthropy practices into your own giving, why not ask the organisations you work with how you can better support them? While traditional multigenerational (perpetual) foundations remain dominant, a growing number of donors are embracing time-limited philanthropy. This “giving while living” ethos — deploying charitable capital within a set timeframe — is gaining significant interest. Recent examples run the gamut, from a mid-size family foundation established to spend out in 10 years, to the Gates Foundation's public announcement to sunset in 2045. More anecdotally, it has become a frequently queried topic for J.P. Morgan Philanthropy Advisors, as donors weigh impact during their lifetime against future legacy. The conversation reflects a growing desire for philanthropists to witness firsthand the impact of their giving and to respond swiftly to urgent social and environmental needs. Though, in some cases, interest can also be attributed to funders recognising that family foundation succession plans are not always viable; for example, if younger generations have different philanthropic interests or prefer to deploy charitable capital in alternative ways. For those considering a spend-down structure, we can learn from the MAVA Foundation, which managed its transition thoughtfully and responsibly. Established in 1994 by Luc Hoffmann, MAVA was designed from the outset to be time-limited, in the belief that future generations should have the freedom to set their own course and adapt to changing needs. Planning for closure began in 2015, giving partners ample time to prepare. Over the eight-year transition, MAVA supported its partners to build resilience and ensured its legacy of purposeful philanthropy would continue through others.7 As more families, individuals and boards build strong relationships with their partners, embrace new technologies and prioritise impact now over legacy later, the template for stewarding charitable capital will become ever more nuanced and innovative. title: HSBC, JP Morgan settle first live digital gold collateral trades - Ledger Insights
content: The World Gold Council announced the first live transactions for Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) between HSBC, JP Morgan and StoneX, a little over a year after it first proposed the concept in a September 2025 white paper. The Wholesale Digital Gold pilot involved trading, settlement and the use of gold as collateral, which is a key driver behind the initiative. ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) is the platform operator and Baton Systems is the technology provider. Gold is a significant market worth around $28 trillion in total, with around half of that considered investable. About $8 trillion is in the form of physical bars, coins, gold ETFs and over the counter private investments, with central banks managing $5 trillion and derivatives worth more than a trillion. The challenge with physical gold is it sits at custodians, and moving it is not that easy. Yet owners want to use it as collateral, and the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is exploring how to make that happen. Pooled Gold Interests aim to combine quick transfers with a proprietary interest in the gold, which might make central counterparties (CCPs) more willing to accept it as collateral. It’s not that gold isn’t currently electronically traded. The challenge is the formats. To transfer gold quickly, most is held “unallocated” with a bank, meaning it is a claim on the bank as opposed to outright ownership of the bars. In London those claims are mainly on Citi, HSBC, ICBC Standard Bank, JP Morgan and UBS. Because of the bank counterparty risk, this form of gold is not eligible as CCP collateral in the UK and EU. By contrast there is far less risk if identified gold bars are held at a custodian, but there’s friction in transferring it. This is referred to as “allocated” gold and CME Clearing is one of the few to accept this as collateral. The World Gold Council’s PGI pilot introduces a third path that addresses the counterparty risk while making gold easier to move and settle. The FCA is expressly exploring gold tokenization. Yet the PGI pilot does not use tokens, even though it uses a distributed ledger. Baton Systems told Ledger Insights the PGIs were created on its permissioned DLT, which also handled the transfers, settlement and the collateral pledge. Baton is known for its Core Collateral and Core FX solutions, with HSBC as an anchor client for Core FX, which is now the foundation of OSTTRA’s PvP offering. Core FX likewise uses DLT for workflow purposes rather than tokens, and several years ago HSBC’s Mark Williamson outlined some of the benefits of sidestepping tokenization to Ledger Insights, noting that tokenization can add an extra settlement step and create fragmented liquidity. Since then HSBC has launched its own gold tokenization offering, both for wholesale clients and for retail in Hong Kong. Want the full story? title: World Gold Council facilitates first live transactions using Pooled Gold Interests - World Gold Council
content: We have recently received reports of impersonation scams involving fraudulent websites and individuals falsely claiming to represent the World Gold Council (WGC). These scams may involve the misuse of our branding or logos, or individuals posing as WGC employees to present fake login pages or false investment opportunities that are not created or endorsed by the World Gold Council.The World Gold Council does not provide investment advice, solicit or sell gold or any other financial products, open customer trading accounts, or request money transfers under any circumstances. If you are contacted by someone claiming to represent the WGC and directed to a website requesting personal or financial information, please assume that it is highly likely to be fraudulent.Please remain vigilant against any communication that appears suspicious. If you receive such contact or believe you may have been the target of a scam, contact your local police station immediately for assistance. LONDON, 24 November 2026 – The World Gold Council announced today that HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX have traded, settled and used Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) as collateral in live, legally binding wholesale-market transactions for the first time. The World Gold Council’s Wholesale Digital Gold initiative is underpinned by PGI, and these pilot transactions mark a significant step towards a new way for institutions to own, transfer and use gold. ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) acted as operator and Baton Systems as technology provider. Loco London physical 400-ounce Good Delivery gold bars were placed into the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem and PGI were created, giving participants proprietary interests over pooled gold. Once the transactions were settled, the gold was withdrawn from the ecosystem, completing the full lifecycle. The Wholesale Digital Gold initiative has developed a new settlement ecosystem for the wholesale gold market, now at pilot stage, in which ownership of segregated physical gold is held and transferred electronically as PGI. It aims to address a longstanding challenge for the industry: how to preserve the integrity and trust of physical gold ownership while making gold easier to trade and use across modern financial markets. It is designed to complement existing allocated and unallocated gold settlement. The pilot demonstrates real progress on how digitalisation can help gold move more efficiently through financial markets. It comes as the FCA considers responses to its Call for Input on tokenised gold in UK wholesale markets, including its potential use as collateral. Together, these developments help strengthen the UK’s position to lead the next generation of gold-market infrastructure. Following the pilot, participating institutions commented on the live test of Pooled Gold Interests: David Tait, Chief Executive Officer, World Gold Council, said: “Today, Wholesale Digital Gold moved from concept to reality. For the first time, leading institutions have transferred, settled and used fractional ownership of physical gold as collateral through real, live transactions. This is a historic step forward for the gold market, preserving trust in physical ownership while opening up new ways for gold to be used in modern financial markets. This kind of significant progress can only be achieved when the industry works together.” Richard Anthony, Global Head of Macro eRisk and Precious Metals, HSBC, said: “HSBC has been participating in the precious metals market for more than 160 years and is one of the world’s largest gold custodians and clearers. We continue to invest in technology, including our gold tokenisation capabilities, to enable our clients to have greater access to gold. Developing a modern digital infrastructure for gold ownership and settlement is important to the overall market.” Mark Amlin, Global Head of Physical Commodities, J.P. Morgan, said: “J.P. Morgan is one of the largest and most active participants in the global precious metals market, with a presence that spans trading, clearing, vaulting and financing across every major hub. That global footprint gives us a clear view of where the market’s infrastructure needs to evolve. Gold ownership that is fractional, readily transferable and insolvency remote would allow gold to be used more widely across financial markets, including as collateral. We were pleased to test that in practice alongside other market participants.” Michael Skinner, Global Head of Metals, StoneX, said: “StoneX has invested consistently in developing new solutions across commodities markets, from vaulting and refining through to execution and clearing, and we support initiatives like this one because they have the potential to deliver materially better outcomes for our clients — greater flexibility, lower operational friction and more efficient use of capital. We are pleased to have been involved from the outset.” “IBA has a track record of anticipating and providing the infrastructure that modern commodity and financial markets require to operate more efficiently, including as the administrator of some of the world’s most important precious metals benchmarks. For new collateral and settlement models to scale, they require certainty and predictability. IBA’s experience providing robust and reliable governance, technology and data management, combined with our whole-market approach, helps build confidence amongst participants and other stakeholders in the infrastructure we provide. We are pleased to act as operator for these pilot transactions and to bring our experience to the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem.” Arjun Jayaram, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Baton Systems, said: “Wholesale Digital Gold requires real-time technology with distinct workflows and data permissions for each participant. We have spent a decade building infrastructure that enables institutions to control and move cash, securities and collateral, and digital gold is a natural extension of that work. We were delighted to help show what a modern, interoperable settlement layer can do for one of the world’s oldest and deepest markets.” This initiative has been developed by the World Gold Council, advised by Linklaters LLP and Hilltop Walk Consulting and was first launched in September 2025 in the White Paper: Pooled Gold Interests and Wholesale Digital Gold – A New Vision for the Gold Market. The World Gold Council continues to invite market participants, regulators and technology providers to engage in this initiative and help shape the future of the gold market. We are a membership organisation that champions the role gold plays as a strategic asset, shaping the future of a responsible and accessible gold supply chain. Our team of experts builds understanding of the use case and possibilities of gold through trusted research, analysis, commentary, and insights. We drive industry progress, shaping policy and setting the standards for a perpetual and sustainable gold market. You can follow the World Gold Council on X at @goldcouncil and LinkedIn. title: Rolls-Royce earnings forecasts lifted by JP Morgan despite lower price target - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results JP Morgan has raised its earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for Rolls-Royce Holdings PLC (LSE:RR.), the aerospace and engineering group, by 4-6% annually between 2027 and 2030. The revisions, averaging around 5% a year, follow the group's November 12 trading update. However, analyst David H Perry, CFA, has reduced the bank's December 2027 sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) price target to 1,650p from 1,800p. The SOTP valuation method assesses a company's individual divisions separately, using comparable businesses to establish their potential worth. JP Morgan's lower target mainly reflects a decline in valuation multiples among listed peers of Rolls-Royce's Power Systems division since August, when the bank last set its price target. Despite the reduction, the revised target still implies approximately 24% upside over the next 13 months, prompting the bank to reiterate its Overweight rating. The contrasting revisions reflect stronger earnings expectations alongside a more conservative valuation of part of the business. Rolls-Royce indicated in its November 12 trading update that it would revisit its medium-term targets when it publishes full-year results in February. The group also plans to accelerate its existing share buyback programme from November 2026, bringing forward purchases of its own shares. The forthcoming medium-term target review could provide further indications of the group's earnings ambitions and its ability to deliver growth across its businesses.
